verdict.rationale: Render's own docs say you can define, deploy, and version your entire architecture with a single YAML file, and the CLI can validate those render.yaml Blueprint files. Independent community users praise the Blueprint spec as simple infrastructure-as-code they keep under version control. missing for 10: in-depth Blueprint spec documentation (which resource types are covered, how a file change syncs to a deploy), detail on the versioning and rollback workflow tied to the YAML file.

support.subject: As a devops-lead, I can define, deploy, and version my entire architecture with a single configuration file

citations.quote: Define, deploy, and version your entire architecture with a single YAML file.
Manage your multi-service architecture with a single YAML file.
One of the biggest appeals to me is their simplified, docker-compose like approach to infrastructure as code... I still like to have it as code under version control
